JFK scholar James DiEugenio joins Danny Jones to talk about secret Kennedy files he says the Pentagon will never free. The episode title calls them top secret. DiEugenio has spent his life on the case and its sealed paper.

DiEugenio names the files he most wants freed and says what he thinks they hold. He argues the state still guards the core of the case after all these years. Jones asks why a case this old still needs such guard. Listeners get a guide to the vault from a man who has fought it for decades. The library holds the talk as an archive record.

Hardcore wrestling fans are the subject of this Danny Jones episode on the faithful who live for the ring. Jones looks at the subculture of devotees who travel, chant, and paint themselves for their heroes. Their devotion goes far past casual watching into a way of life.

The episode follows fans whose whole calendar bends around shows and storylines. It explores what the spectacle gives them: belonging, heroes, and a story that never ends. Jones treats the marks, as fans call themselves, with respect rather than mockery. Curious listeners get a look at the soul of a loud, loyal world.
podcast-joerogan-DsiKEBAFmm4:
Travis Walton tells his alien abduction story in a segment of the Joe Rogan Experience, in his own words. In 1975, Walton vanished for five days after his logging crew reported a craft in an Arizona forest. His case became one of the most famous of its kind.

Walton recounts the light, the missing days, and the polygraph fights that followed him for decades. Rogan asks what the attention did to his life and whether he would take it back. Whether a listener believes a word, the segment preserves the man's own telling of a story that never let him go.
podcast-joerogan-kyjOAD3FQm4:
Musician and comedian Reggie Watts joins Joe Rogan to muse on UFOs and to share the tale of his own sighting. Watts is known for improvised music and off-beat humor. His show visits tend to roam far and fast.

Watts tells what he saw in the sky and how it has stayed with him since. He and Rogan bat around what the craft could be, from state tech to guests from far stars. The mood stays light even as the topic runs deep. Listeners get a playful mind on a strange tale. The library holds the segment as an archive record.
podcast-joerogan-uYO2fJ-M_M4:
Writer and director Taylor Sheridan joins Joe Rogan for episode 2517. Sheridan created Yellowstone and a string of modern westerns. His shows rule cable with tales of land and power.

Rogan explores how a failed actor became a top storyteller. Sheridan talks about ranch life, research, and writing fast. They discuss the real West behind the drama. The episode will please fans of his shows and writers alike. It shows how one man's love of horses and hard country became an empire of stories. Craft, not luck, is his theme from start.
podcast-tuckercarlson-eqNCHt3GRm4:
A social media adviser to President Trump reveals inside details in this Tucker Carlson episode. The adviser discusses the Epstein files, the standoff with Iran, and commentator Mark Levin's advocacy for Israel. Carlson bills the hour as a tell-all from inside Trump's online operation.

The guest explains how the team handles breaking fights and hostile coverage in real time. He shares his view of the pressure campaigns around Iran policy and the Epstein releases. Carlson asks who inside the movement pushes which message and why. Political and curious viewers get an insider spilling on the message wars.
